ai.description: This lizard reaches a snout-vent length of 7–8 cm. It is brownish-grey with a distinct white nuchal stripe and a prominent, spiny crest extending from the head to the mid-back.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Monilesaurus acanthocephalus* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, enlarged, spine-like scale located directly above the tympanum.
ai.habitat: *Monilesaurus acanthocephalus* inhabits the high-altitude montane shola forests and surrounding grasslands of the southern Western Ghats, typically above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Monilesaurus acanthocephalus* is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates among leaf litter and low-hanging vegetation during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Monilesaurus acanthocephalus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 5–9 eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months, typically from April to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Monilesaurus acanthocephalus* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats of India, specifically occurring in the high-elevation shola-grassland mosaics of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
